sections.title: TCP in One Line
sections.body: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) first builds a connection, then delivers everything exactly once and in order — like a phone call: you say hello, wait for hi back, then talk.

sections.title: The 3-Way Handshake
sections.body: Before any real data moves, both sides agree to talk:
sections.code:
Client  --SYN---->        Server
        ("want to talk?")
Client  <--SYN+ACK--      Server
        ("sure, you talk too")
Client  --ACK---->        Server
        ("great, starting!")

sections.title: How TCP Stays Reliable
points: Sequence numbers — every byte is counted, so order is known.
Retransmission — no ACK came back? Send it again.
Flow control (windowing) — receiver says how much it can handle.
Duplicates are dropped — app never gets the same data twice.

sections.title: Closing Politely
sections.body: TCP ends a session with a 4-step goodbye so nothing is cut off mid-sentence:
sections.code:
FIN --> ACK <-- FIN <-- ACK -->
(both sides agree to hang up)

sections.title: Where TCP Shines
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: SYN -> SYN/ACK -> ACK. If a question mentions reliability, ordering or handshakes, the answer is TCP.
